### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3572509b92e9903e67e0f45ffe86dd5263a0774` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `dc6e969931ae51169ddbd4aa145f47de7b48ffae` — the merge of head `8bdde034ce3b4bc3094bc418c7754ceb7dbf018a` into base `b3572509b92e9903e67e0f45ffe86dd5263a0774`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin dc6e969931ae51169ddbd4aa145f47de7b48ffae && git checkout dc6e969931ae51169ddbd4aa145f47de7b48ffae
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b3572509b92e9903e67e0f45ffe86dd5263a0774 8bdde034ce3b4bc3094bc418c7754ceb7dbf018a && git checkout -B drift-repro b3572509b92e9903e67e0f45ffe86dd5263a0774 && git merge --no-ff 8bdde034ce3b4bc3094bc418c7754ceb7dbf018a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3572509b92e9903e67e0f45ffe86dd5263a0774
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b3572509b92e9903e67e0f45ffe86dd5263a0774` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8bdde034ce3b4bc3094bc418c7754ceb7dbf018a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.extension-field-suffix.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts (`judgeExtensionFieldSuffix`, `extensionFieldSuffixRefusalError`, `objectBodyExtensionFieldSuffixRefusal`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts (`promoteDraft`, `assertAllowed`, `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts (`overrideWriteVerdict`, the `declared_object` arm), packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts (`isExtensionFieldName`), packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts (`isCustomizationPackage`, `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION.object`), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the `adopt-orphans` route), packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts (`errorFromThrown`), docs/adr/0146 D10 and D11 — all read at the head, none reviewed. Not reviewed: `.changeset/28735-adopt-orphans-extension-field-suffix.md` (prose face, read for ②).

Inputs: card #28735 body and its two comments (claim `6560803591`, os-dev-report `6562074496`), PR #28724's contract review `6560407046` (the filing record), PR #28768 body, file list and net diff against `main` at the merge base `7a48bf73f5` (three files: the changeset, `protocol.ts` +43/-2, the test file +80/-1; the mid-run merge of #28734 leaves no other hunk), and the 48 check-runs on the head: 36 success, 12 skipped (UI, docs, dogfood shards, live temporal, opt-in harnesses), 0 failures. `Check Changeset` (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration` and `check-changeset-no-major`), `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and every `Lint ·` / `Type Check ·` family are among the green runs.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

1. **The adopt door asks the judge against the target** (`protocol.ts:26832-26854`, `reassignOrphanedMetadata`). After `refuseOrganizationScopedWrite` (ADR-0131 D6, first) and the orphan read, and before the first `engine.update`, every orphan row whose `canonicalMetaType` is `object` and whose `state` is `active` is handed to `judgeExtensionFieldSuffix({ packageId: request.targetPackageId, objects })` keyed by `row.name` with `name` overwritten to the row's; a non-empty answer throws `extensionFieldSuffixRefusalError` before the loop. Right: it is the one exported judge the card names, the call `duplicatePackage` makes (`:26235-26249`, same shape, same unparseable-row rule), `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 with `issues[]` at `objects.NAME.fields.FIELD` (the duplicate door's path shape, since many objects are judged at once; the save door's `fields.FIELD` is the single-body form). Refused whole: `reassigned` is still empty and `applyRegistryWriteThrough` is below the throw (pinned: `engine.update` and the write-through never called, both rows still unbound). A target that is a `.custom` pair is not judged (`isCustomizationPackage`, judge line 139), so an adoption into the base's pair is admitted (pinned, `reassignedCount: 1`, row rebound to the pair). Right.
2. **The type fold.** The orphan filter folds through `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` (`:26826`), the judge block and the loop's registry limb through `canonicalMetaType` (`:563`, `canonicalMetaUrlType`); both answer `object` for `objects`. Right, and the same two spellings the loop already used.
3. **Drafts are not judged at the adopt door** (ruling 1 names active rows). An adopted package-less draft is rebound in storage only, as before; at promotion `promoteDraftForPublish` judges `draftForGate.body` against `promoteInto` (`:23910-23915`), and the repository promotes under `draftPackageId ?? adoptInto` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:1574`), so a draft rebound to a plain package is judged against that package when it would go live. Right: no draft reaches the runtime without the promotion (ADR-0048), and the promotion keeps the judge.
4. **The promotion's suffix block is seal-gated** (`:23910`): `draftForGate && singularType === 'object' && !this.isSealedManagedItem(singularType, request.name)`, byte-for-byte the D9.9 (`:23834`) and namespace-prefix (`:23870`) conditions. Right, and it takes no capability away, read through the store: `isSealedManagedItem` is `isArtifactBacked && !registryAllowsOverlay(type)` (`:16219`); for an `object` the override gate can never `admit` (`OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION.object` is `extend_only`, `customization-package.ts:341`, so `overrideWriteVerdict` answers `declared_object`, `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts:305-308`), so `declaredOverride` is false and `intent` is `override-artifact` for every artifact-backed object (`:24066`); `promoteDraft` passes that intent to `put` (`:1604`), and `assertAllowed` (`:2341-2407`) reaches `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403 for it (or the read-only-base door above it), with the `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` hatch opening only `runtime-only`. Both `OVERLAY_ALLOWED_TYPES` sets derive from the registry's `allowEnvironmentOverlay` (`protocol.ts:15745`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts:408`), so the protocol's "sealed" and the store's seal name the same rows. A sealed draft carrying `x__c` therefore never goes live with the judge skipped; it gets the store's one answer (pinned: `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403, draft kept). The `singularType === 'object'` term changes nothing (`objectBodyExtensionFieldSuffixRefusal` answers `undefined` for any other type). Right.
5. **No public surface moves.** `index.ts` is untouched; no new export, type, error code or spec file; the REST route (`packages.ts:2577-2607`) is unchanged and relays the throw through `deps.errorFromThrown` (`http-dispatcher.ts:1254`, `resolveThrownHttpError` carries `status` and `code`), the relay the duplicate door's refusal already rides. Right, and it is why the declaration is `no (narrowing)`, not `yes (narrowing)` as #28724's was.
6. **The namespace-prefix and owner judges are not added** at this door. Right as a scope reading of ruling 2 ("say whether"); judged in ③.
7. The judge module's header (`protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts:10-20`) lists the doors that call it and does not name the adopt door; the test file's header does. Outside the claim's file surface; see ④, should-fix (prose).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, the one package the diff moves; BREAKING banner; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a requirement tightened at one more door of the rule #28564 declared `narrowed`); one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with the measured count (0 fields spelled `[a-z0-9]__c` outside tests) and the migration paragraph (rename, or adopt into the pair). AGENTS.md rule 3: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves; `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and carries its disposition. Matches what the diff publishes. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, identical on the PR body and the changeset: the accept set narrows (judgment ①.1) and no public surface widens (①.5). The card prescribed this line. Right. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are green on the head.
- No `skip-changeset`; one released package publishes. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (should the namespace-prefix and owner judges ride the same pre-loop call): the dev recommends A, one card for both with a reach measurement first. **Answered: A.** Read in the tree, the namespace judge's envelope is `NAMESPACE_PREFIX` / 422 (`:23870-23878`), not the suffix judge's `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, so one adoption could fail two ways and needs an ordering ruling; and a package-less object is usually unprefixed, so adopting into a namespaced base would be refused for most environments, which turns the ADR-0070 D5 convergence door into a dead end unless the adopt also renames, a design question, not a gap-closure. The owner judge alone is too small for its own narrowing record. **Escalated to the seat**: file one card for both judges at the adopt door, its first step the reach count over the CRM and showcase examples; `out_of_scope_findings[1]` is the same item.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (the judge module's door list): outside the claim's file surface, left by the claim's own rule. Named in ④ as a should-fix so it has a carrier.
- Dev flags: the mid-run merge of #28734 (`protocol.ts` read sites) — the net diff against the merge base holds only this PR's hunks, so the merge is clean as reported. The first gate pass's three PREREQUISITE exits and one queue-timeout at `6f6d2f35` measured nothing; the head's check-runs answer those families green. No flag left open.
- Claim constraints held: no `packages/spec/**`, no `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, no `stored-row-binding.ts`, no `withRowBinding`, no automation boot pull in the file list; PR carries no assignee and no governance label.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real. ADR-0146 D10 says the suffix "is refused in a non-`.custom` package at publish"; on `main` the adopt door was the one write that made a package-less `x__c` row a plain package's live own field without any publish (the filing record's first should-fix). No declared capability is taken away at a consumer: D11 keeps a package-less row for an item no package ships as environment metadata, and the save door still admits it unbound (unchanged, re-pinned by the new tests' setup); what closes is the rebind into a plain package, which D10 never granted. The pair target is admitted at the door (pinned), the clean row into a plain package moves (pinned), and the count in the tree is 0 fields. Each door keeps its own envelope; no code is minted; no spec file moves.

Break attempts, in the tree:

- **The seal gate opening a hole** (a sealed object draft promoted with the suffix judge skipped and the store admitting it): not reachable, judgment ①.4; the store's seal and the protocol's predicate read the same registry flag, and an object override never `admit`s.
- **A draft escaping both doors**: an adopted package-less draft is judged at its promotion against its new binding (①.3); `publishPackageDrafts` promotes through the same method; the restore doors keep their own call. Holds.
- **Half-moved adoptions**: the throw precedes the loop, `reassigned` is empty, nothing is written through; the `console.error` sentence "run the adoption again — it is idempotent" stays true. Holds.
- **The `sys_metadata` sentinel rows**: included by the orphan filter and judged like a NULL binding. Holds.
- **Message cap**: one sentence plus "(N more fields in `issues`)", bounded whatever the orphan count. Holds.
- **A package-less `object_extension` row carrying an unsuffixed or suffixed field, adopted**: not judged at this door, and not at the save door either (`objectBodyExtensionFieldSuffixRefusal` is object-only); #28724's review assigned the runtime `object_extension` write door to #28574 (open). Same class, that card's; not a finding of this PR.
- **Should-fix (prose, one line).** `protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts`'s header names every door that calls the judge and omits `reassignOrphanedMetadata`; the next edit of that file adds the adopt door to the list, as the test file's header already does.

No must-fix.

**VERDICT: PASS**
